subject: Life Skills
title: Social Loafing
description: Learn Social Loafing in one minute.

hook.text: French engineer Ringelmann found that people pull a rope 50% less hard in a group than when pulling alone.

buildup.text: Social loafing happens when individual effort is invisible. If nobody tracks your contribution.

discovery.text: The bigger the group, the worse it gets. In a group of eight, individual effort drops to about 49% of their solo.

twist.text: It is not laziness. People genuinely believe they are contributing fairly. The drop is unconscious and often sincere.

climax.text: Make individual contributions visible. Assign named tasks, not shared ones. Accountability kills loafing instantly.

punchline.text: Named tasks, visible owners. Loafing disappears.

quiz.question: What is the main cause of social loafing?
options: People are inherently lazy in groups
Individual contributions are invisible, so effort drops unconsciously
Groups always have one dominant member who does all the work
